How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the
following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to
the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person
per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to
address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website. Public
Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

  This report provides a summary of the Proposed Budget and Capital
  Improvement Plan (CIP) for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. City-wide operating
  revenues and expenditures total $94,079,000 and $91,616,000, respectively.
  The General Fund comprises revenues of $51,585,000 and expenditures of
  $50,185,000, for a positive net change in fund balance of $1,400,000. The city-
  wide expenditure figures include $16,701,000 for new capital improvement
  projects.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide direction to staff on certain
  presented budget augmentations, the planned City special events for the
  upcoming fiscal year, and other items for the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 budget.

 3. ADJOURNMENT

  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will

  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF MAY 4, 2023

  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at

  5:36 P.M. on Thursday, May 4, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission

  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan,  Tony Ding,  Denise  Menchaca,  Vice  Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.

  Council Members Absent:  None.

  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney

  Paul Early, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Publ ic Works Director/ City

  Engineer  Greg  de Vinck,  Fire  Chief  Steven  Wallace,

  Human  Resources/ Risk Management  Director Edward

  Macias,  Finance  Director  William  Kaholokula,

  Director

  and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Dr. Chasity Jennings- Nunez provided comments questioning  special- event funding

  and recommending the City fund a social services manager and a City Birthday event.

  Jeanne Raya, resident, requested clarification of legal services expenses.

  City Manager Lazzaretto provided a detailed breakdown of the City Attorney category

  components and costs.

  2.  STUDY SESSION

I  A. PROPOSED BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-2024

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Discussion  included  consideration  of the following:  an additional  police officer

  position; a new public safety facility; future increases in public safety staffing needs;

  an additional rescue ambulance plus six paramedic positions; a new fire truck with

  12 additional  staff positions;  a fund for a new K-9 unit; hybridization  of police

  position  for grants;  add- ons to existing  special  events  instead  of adding  new

  events;  setting  money  aside  for Mission  Playhouse  non- profit status  and  an

  endowment;  addition of a part- time development staff position for the Mission

  Playhouse;  formation and staffing for a non- profit committee in support of the

  Mission Playhouse;  details of Capital Improvement  Program Park Fund balance;

  Fa(ade Improvement and Kitchen Start -up  programs; public -private partnerships

  for special  events;  Farmer' s Market, fireworks,  Lantern  Festival , Moon Festival ,

  Veteran 's Day and Memorial Day events; and mental health programming .

I  RE CESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed  at 8:02 P.M . and reconvened  at 8:11  P.M. with all Council

  Members present.

  Discussion  continued  on  an  app for City  news  and  for reporting  issues ; an

  upcoming staff discussion on pop- up events and temporary permits; potential for
  the City to be a fiber- optic provider; soliciting ideas for programming  from the

  public;  resuming  Youth  in  Government  programming;  overnight  parking

  regulations  as a separate discussion  item outside of the budget discussion ; and

  appreciation for budget clarity improving each year.

  3.  ADJ OURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:37 P.M .
